newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News-Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News-Sept 18.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The dust settles in the Australian Football League as Hawthorn's Operation Payback anti-merger faction is set to take control at Glenferrie Oval after the incumbent board yesterday announced it would resign following the defeat of its pro-merger stance by passionate members. Page 24.

Stephen Thornton, Queensland rugby union's new chief executive, has warned Australian teams were under threat of cashed-up English clubs looking to buy our best talent. Thornton also said he expected a national union club competition to start in Australia as early as next year. Page 23.

John O'Neill, Australian Rugby Union boss, continues to fight to set up a Grand Slam tour of Britain and Ireland by the Wallabies in November. Although setting up the deal has been plagued with problems, O'Neill is highly confident the tour will go-ahead. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Football League commission has taken a tough stance on mergers despite the failed Melbourne-Hawthorn attempt. Ross Oakley, AFL chief executive, has insisted Victoria cannot continue to support 10 clubs and following Monday night's events, lcubs would now have to be in more serious trouble than Melbourne and Hawthorn for a merger to take place. Page 44.

Sydney Swans AFL star Tony Lockett's 40-minute training session came to a stop last night when he could not complete an exercise. Coach Rodney Eade said Lockett felt his groin injury coming back but he should still play on Saturday. Page 44.

Selection for the position of coach for the Australian men's and women's hockey teams is set to start. Amongst the six applicants to the Australian Hockey Association for the men's team and the 10 applicants for the Hockeyroos, it is believed current Women's Hockey Australia coach Ric Charlesworth has applied for both postings. Page 45.
THE AGE

As the fallout from Monday night's dramatic Australian Football League Melbourne-Hawthorn merger continues, anti-merger advocate Joseph Gutnick will meet Melbourne president Ian Ridley today seeking to wrest the presidency from Ridley, and install his Demon Alternative running mate, Brian Dixon, as his deputy. Page C16.

Australian Football League merger outcast Hawthorn was buoyed yesterday by the news that sports marketing firm, International Management Group, has approached the club to consider playing a key marketing and sponsorship role. IMG's managing director James Erskine will begin discussions with president-elect Ian Dicker next week. Page C16.

Australian Davis Cup captain John Newcombe predicts a "biff-up" when his team of Jason Stoltenberg and Mark Philippoussis takes on Croatia in front of a hostile tennis crowd in Split later this week. Australia must win the tie to regain its place in the elite World Group. Page C15.
HERALD SUN

The world's largest management group, IMG, has been appointed to take over the affairs of successful Melbourne-based race-horse trainer Lee Freedman and his brothers. The Freedman stable is the first racing organisation in Australia to enlist the full-time services of a management company. Page 78.

Champion Brisbane Bears utility Michael Voss and ruckman Peter Clark's ankle and Achilles injuries have subsided and both players have declared themselves ready to play against North Melbourne in Saturday's AFL finals clash, meanwhile, North's still beliees winger Stuart Anderson can recover from an injured hamstring in time for the match. Page 78.

The Lure of A$61,000 is sure to motivate the financially embattled Magic when it takes on North Melbourne in the second last game of basketball's Foxtel Cup. In good form and following a hectic schedule, the Magic defeated Newcastle a week ago and picked up $20,000 before defeating Hobart on Sunday. Page 73.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Rugby league's David Barnhill, Terry Hill, Brett Dallas and Billy Moore are likely to play next week although it is unlikely they will last next week's play-offs. St George's Barnhill and Manly's Hill are recovering from ankle injuries while North Sydney' Dallas and Moore have foot and hamstring problems. Page 80.

Sydney Swans full-forward Tony Lockett is still expected to play in Saturday night's preliminary final against Australian Football League finals hopefuls Essendon, despite the flare-up of his groin injury at practice last night. Page 73.

Australia's Socceroos must confront Phil Masinga, Eric Tinkler and the altitude in Johannesburg if they are to overcome South Africa in their second match of tomorrow morning's (AEST) Four Nations Tournament. Australian coach Eddie Thomson will field the same side that recorded a 2-0 win over Ghana. Page 72.
